annotation.title_clean: Ethics and Representation of Robots in Literatures
annotation.title_en: Ethics and Representation of Robots in Literatures
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Journal of the Robotics Society of Japan (author not stated in excerpt)
annotation.venue: Journal of the Robotics Society of Japan
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical article in the Journal of the Robotics Society of Japan examining the etymology of mechanism, android and automaton and the role of automata in Greek myth. It argues that literary representations of robots, including Asimov's three laws, carry inherent ethical problems and should be set aside when building practical robot ethics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot ethics discussions draw on images of robots from literature and science fiction.
Etymology of mechanism, android and automaton reveals hidden ethical problems.
Automata in Greek drama play tragic roles that bring misfortune to humans.
Practical robot ethics should intentionally ignore literary representations.
Asimov's three laws should not be the basis of realistic robot ethics.
